scenes.vo: (a price markup) plus a fee. network fees, called "gas") and some U.S.D.C. (a dollar stablecoin for practice). Deposit your money, usually by bank transfer (cheapest) or card (fastest, most expensive). Instant buy / convert buttons are simple but often include a spread The trading screen ("advanced" or "spot trading") uses an order book: Market order: buy now at the best available price Limit order: buy only at your chosen price or better. It often has a lower fee ("maker" fee).

lines: Why keep a little ETH even if you mostly want stablecoins?
scenes.sub: Answer: You need ETH to pay network fees (gas) on Ethereum and most of its low-cost networks.

lines: Market or limit order: which controls the price you pay?
scenes.vo: Market or limit order: which controls the price you pay? ... Pause and think. ... The answer: A limit order.
scenes.cap: Market or limit order: which controls the price you pay? Pause and think. The answer: A limit order.

lines: Why keep records from day one?
scenes.sub: Answer: Most countries tax crypto gains. Records of dates, amounts, prices and fees make that straightforward.
